text:
jess: Hey — hitting something odd in a sample app using the Go generator streaming API. After cancelling the parent ctx I still see goroutines stuck.

jess: Minimal pattern: I iterate a stream and launch goroutines per chunk,
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()

stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }

for i, chunk := range stream.Iterator() {
    go func() {
        // process chunk asynchronously
        fmt.Println(i, chunk.Text)
    }()
}

// I expect cancel() to cause Iterator() loop to exit and goroutines to stop,
// but `ps` shows leftover goroutines holding onto the stream's internals.
```

jess: Any ideas if I'm misusing the SDK or if this is a bug?

alex: Two quick things — one is the classic loop-variable capture in Go.
You're capturing `i` and `chunk` by reference if you don't pass them into the closure.

alex: Try: `for i, chunk := range stream.Iterator() { i, chunk := i, chunk; go func(i int, c Chunk) { ... }(i, chunk) }`

sam: Also worth checking whether `stream.Iterator()` spawns an internal goroutine that needs `Close()` when you cancel. Some earlier SDKs required calling `stream.Close()` or `stream.Err()` to drain.

matt: I ran into something similar. Two actionable checks: 1) do you call `cancel()` from another goroutine or return from the function? If the function exits without waiting for your worker goroutines they might still be alive. 2) ensure the stream's context is the one you're cancelling (no accidental background ctx).

jess: Good catch on the closure — I overlooked that. After changing to pass vars into the func I still had ~2 goroutines left. They look like:

```
goroutine 123 [chan receive]:
github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/gen/stream.(*internalIterator).run
...
```

jess: So maybe the iterator's run loop isn't noticing ctx.Done() immediately.

alex: If it's the internal iterator, there was a known window where the read goroutine blocks on a socket read and doesn't select on ctx.Done(). We've got a fix on main that adds a short read deadline + select on the ctx to unblock.

sam: Workarounds: 1) call `stream.Close()` after canceling, 2) expose a `stream.Drain()` helper in the sample app to ensure the iterator goroutine exits. Both are hacky but help until the runtime fix lands.

matt: I'd also add a test in the generator integration tests that cancels mid-stream and asserts no goroutines leaked after a small wait. That will catch regressions.

jess: Thanks. I'll: 1) fix the closure usage in the sample, 2) add explicit `defer stream.Close()` and 3) add a unit that cancels mid-stream to the sampleapp CI.

jess: Quick question — is `stream.Close()` safe to call from a different goroutine than the one that created the stream? Docs don't say.

alex: Yes, Close should be thread-safe. But we'll doc it explicitly.

ci-bot: FYI I ran the sampleapp e2e on your branch and saw the leak reproduce: 3 goroutines after cancel (timeout 5s).

sam: I'll pick up the SDK fix to select on ctx.Done() during socket reads — PR incoming. In the meantime I'll add an example in devex samples showing the safe pattern: `defer stream.Close()` + pass loop vars into goroutines.

matt: Also consider adding a `Stream.WithContext(ctx)` helper on client creation so users don't accidentally mix contexts. Less foot-gunning.

jess: Awesome. Creating PR for sampleapp now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/742 — includes closure fix, defer Close, and a small CI test.

alex: Nice. Once the SDK PR lands can you re-run the CI test and drop a follow-up note here? :thumbsup:

jess: Will do. Thanks everyone :rocket:
